context:
Found 2026-10-17 at site-split closeout (follow-up list in site-split-99).

Moved from the BenchBox core tracker on 2026-10-30, when this repository gained its own tracker.

2026-11-02: Owner decision: retire MyST now. Core docs use 159 {toctree} blocks (they drive the site sidebar and docs index), 17 {tags} blocks and `(label)=` targets in 158 files; the converter is 3,331 lines, part of which serves plain Markdown too. Retirement needs a replacement navigation source, a core docs conversion PR, then removal of the MyST handlers here once a bundle with converted docs reaches the site.

2026-11-02: Premise corrected: since site PR #66 the published docs are authored in benchbox-site/docs/; core keeps only 17 unrendered {tags} blocks and one hidden toctree, so retirement is site-side plus a small core cleanup, no bundle schema change. The converter stays as the plain-Markdown pipeline. Owner decisions: docs/nav.yml navigation; flatten section index lists; front matter tags; keep old label and {#id} anchors as <span id>; retire objects.inv; keep duplicate sidebar entries; retire docs:parity; keep heading-id algorithm; permanent MyST guard; native blog index; core PR limited to leftover blocks. Plan: three site PRs (add support with byte-identical output; convert content; delete MyST handlers) and one core PR.
description:
The site build converts core's MyST docs at build time with a custom converter (benchbox-site website/src/converter/build.ts, document.ts, handlers/, inventory.ts, plus website/scripts/myst-inventory.ts and inventory/expected-removals-rst-to-myst.json). It was built for the Astro migration (astro-site-31) while Sphinx still rendered the same sources. Sphinx is gone from core since #3096, so the converter is now the only renderer and the MyST dialect is kept only for it.

Decide: keep MyST and the converter, or convert core docs to plain Markdown/MDX once and delete the converter. Record the choice with its cost (core tests that lock doc text, README links, benchbox/utils/version.py reading docs/README.md).
